chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Rabie, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Take the pebbles for pelting the Jamarah from Jam', and if you take them from your place of departure in Mina, it will suffice you.

key_terms.أَجْزَأَكَ: it will suffice you / be valid for you
key_terms.جَمْعٌ: Jam', a place near Muzdalifah where pilgrims collect pebbles

ai.seo_question: Where should pilgrims collect their pebbles for casting at the Jamarat during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the flexibility in sourcing pebbles for the Ramy al-Jamarat, affirming that while Jam' is the primary location, taking them from one's own luggage in Mina is equally valid. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease (yusr) in ritual acts, allowing pilgrims to avoid unnecessary hardship during the busy days of Hajj. It reflects the broader juristic principle that the validity of the act depends on the intention and the object's nature rather than strict geographical constraints.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Rabie, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Take the pebbles (for pelting) Al-Jamarah, from Jam’a (place of assembly near Muzdalifah); and if you were to take from your departure in Mina, it would suffice you’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad from Rib’iy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Take the pebbles for al-Jamar from Jam‘ and if you take them from your lodging in Mina’ is also sufficient.’”
